# graphs4u

> Free, open-source, browser-based graph algorithm visualizer. Users draw a graph (nodes and edges, optionally directed and/or weighted) directly on a canvas and run classic graph algorithms on it, seeing every visited node and edge highlighted, plus the numeric result. No account, no install, no data leaves the browser.

- **Site:** https://graphs4u.com/
- **Repository:** https://github.com/andradenathan/graphs4u.com
- **License:** MIT
- **Languages:** English (https://graphs4u.com/), Portuguese (https://graphs4u.com/pt/)
- **Runs entirely client-side:** graphs are never uploaded to a server.

## What it does

Users place nodes on a board, connect them with edges, choose whether the graph is directed and whether edges carry weights, then pick an algorithm and a source node (and a target node, for A* and maximum flow). The result is shown on the board and as text, and can be exported to PDF. Any graph can be shared as a link, since the whole graph is encoded in the URL.

## Algorithms available

| Algorithm | Purpose | Time complexity | Needs weights | Negative weights | Page |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BFS (breadth-first search) | Traversal, shortest path in unweighted graphs | O(V + E) | No | N/A | https://graphs4u.com/algorithms/bfs/ |
| DFS (depth-first search) | Traversal, cycle detection | O(V + E) | No | N/A | https://graphs4u.com/algorithms/dfs/ |
| Dijkstra | Single-source shortest path | O((V + E) log V) | Yes | No | https://graphs4u.com/algorithms/dijkstra/ |
| Bellman-Ford | Single-source shortest path, negative cycle detection | O(V · E) | Yes | Yes | https://graphs4u.com/algorithms/bellman-ford/ |
| A* | Shortest path between two nodes, guided by a heuristic | O((V + E) log V) worst case | Yes | No | https://graphs4u.com/algorithms/a-star/ |
| Floyd-Warshall | All-pairs shortest paths | O(V³) | Yes | Yes | https://graphs4u.com/algorithms/floyd-warshall/ |
| Kruskal | Minimum spanning tree | O(E log E) | Yes | Yes | https://graphs4u.com/algorithms/kruskal/ |
| Prim | Minimum spanning tree | O(E log V) | Yes | Yes | https://graphs4u.com/algorithms/prim/ |
| Topological sort | Linear ordering of a DAG | O(V + E) | No | N/A | https://graphs4u.com/algorithms/topological-sort/ |
| Connected components | Groups of mutually reachable nodes | O(V + E) | No | N/A | https://graphs4u.com/algorithms/connected-components/ |
| Maximum flow (Edmonds-Karp) | Largest flow from source to sink | O(V · E²) | Yes (capacities) | No | https://graphs4u.com/algorithms/max-flow/ |

Portuguese versions live under https://graphs4u.com/pt/algoritmos/ with translated slugs (for example `ordenacao-topologica`, `componentes-conexos`, `fluxo-maximo`, `a-estrela`).

## Common questions

**Is graphs4u free?** Yes. It is free and open source under the MIT license, with no account and no paid tier.

**Does it work offline?** Yes, it is a static client-side application and can be installed as a PWA.

**Which algorithm should I use for shortest path?** Use BFS for unweighted graphs, Dijkstra for non-negative weights, A* when you only need one specific source-target pair and have a distance estimate, and Bellman-Ford when any edge weight can be negative or you need negative-cycle detection.

**Kruskal or Prim for a minimum spanning tree?** Both give a minimum spanning tree of the same total weight. Kruskal sorts edges globally and suits sparse graphs; Prim grows a tree from one source node and suits dense graphs.

**How do I share a graph?** The share button copies a link containing the entire graph encoded in the query string, so the recipient opens the exact same graph without any account.

**Can I import my own graph?** Yes, through DOT (Graphviz), an adjacency matrix or an edge list. The same formats can be exported.

## Keyboard shortcuts

`V` select · `N` add node · `E` add edge · `D` delete · `Del`/`Backspace` delete selection · `Esc` clear selection · `Shift + click` multi-select · scroll to zoom.
